title: Sign-in strategy is a fixed-shape config surface
description: Clerk supports multiple sign-in strategies (email link, email code, password, phone code, OAuth via named providers, SAML). The project's Clerk instance is configured to enable one or more of them; the blueprint fixes the SHAPE of that configuration on the project side as a single `signInStrategy` config record owned by `TAC-1001-security-auth-clerk-middleware.interfaces.config` (the field is the `signInStrategy` record on that interface) rather than fixing the CHOICE. The values in the record are Clerk's currently-documented strategy identifiers (as printed by the Clerk dashboard or the Clerk SDK's strategy enumeration at the project's build time). The project's sign-in surface reads the config record and does not hard-code any strategy string; changing the enabled strategy set is a config edit and a Clerk-dashboard change, not a codebase change. Because Clerk hosts every sign-in, sign-up, and MFA UI surface, the blueprint contributes the `hostedIdentityUi` capability: no project route renders a credential-input form of its own; the project route mounts the Clerk-hosted component or redirects to the Clerk-hosted route named by the `signInStrategy` record.
rationale: Fixing the shape leaves the choice open to the operator without leaving the codebase full of hard-coded strategy strings that drift as Clerk's vocabulary drifts. A project that starts on email link and later adds SAML for enterprise is a config bump, not a fork of the sign-in surface. Fixing the choice at the blueprint layer would be premature at the rcf-lite tier where the operator's requirements around sign-in shape are project-specific.
